title: Celestis postmortem / incident follow-up
summary: Follow-up on the 2026-08-12 production outage impacting inference latency and timeouts for Celestis. Reviewed root cause (cache eviction + autoscale race), mitigations deployed, monitoring gaps, and runbook improvements. Agreed next steps: share formal RCA doc, prioritize runbook additions and alert tuning, schedule a dry-run of failover and a small dedicated capacity pilot for critical routes.
next_steps: Samir to send formal RCA doc and incident timeline (by 2026-08-18)
Ava to share proposed runbook edits and alert threshold recommendations (by 2026-08-20)
Celestis to schedule DR dry-run with Redwood (target week of 2026-08-31)
Samir to propose Dedicated pilot config and cost estimate (by 2026-08-21)
Priya to confirm audit log retention and KMS requirements; share policy doc

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-15
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Ava (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM), Maya (Celestis VP Eng), Eric (SRE), Priya (Security), Jonas (Eng)

00:00 Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll keep this tight, just follow up from last week's outage, want to confirm RCA and next steps
00:12 Maya: yeah thanks Samir, appreciate you coordinating. we had another customer exec question this morning about "what actually failed" so we want the timeline and mitigation details to share internally
00:25 Ava: cool, i'll start w the quick tl;dr — root cause was a combination of KV cache thrash after a config change + an autoscaler race on the dedicated pool that delayed pod warmup, so a spike in cold KV loads led to token level timeouts and cascading queueing
00:45 Eric: yeah, from our side we saw the tails hit 5-6s and then a bunch of 504s to the app layer; the app retried a few times which made the surface area worse
00:59 Samir: to be clear, the config change was the cache TTL reduction you pushed on 8/11?
01:05 Maya: right, we set a shorter TTL to reduce staleness, but we didn't anticipate the eviction pattern interacting w the long-running seq workloads
01:18 Ava: exactly; and the autoscaler used a pod cold-start window that wasn't aligned w the model warmup — so we got a window where requests were routed to new pods without warmed KV and that increased latency a lot
01:35 Priya: quick question on the security side: were any logs lost during the event? we need to know for our audit timeline
01:42 Liam: i can answer that — from what we gathered the audit logs were buffered and persisted, we didn't lose acceptance events, but retention was short and you need longer S3 lifecycle to satisfy compliance
01:55 Samir: good — we will give a formal log export with the event IDs in the RCA
02:10 Jonas: there was also some confusion about fallback policies — i thought Redwood would route to a lower-capacity model but it didn't happen?
02:20 Ava: right, the fallback rule was misconfigured; the policy existed but was scoped to a different route name (typo). that's on us, we've fixed the config and added tests to the rollout pipeline
02:35 Eric: ok so what mitigations did you deploy in the immediate window?
02:40 Samir: timeline: at 11:03 we rolled back the cache TTL to prior value, at 11:12 we paused the autoscaler and added a temporary pre-warmed pool, at 11:35 we updated fallback routing and cleared the queue; error rates dropped by 70% within 20 minutes
02:55 Maya: that matches our incident board notes. the only worry from exec was the 25 minute window where our customer-facing dashboards were wrong
03:10 Ava: right, and for that we're proposing two medium-term fixes: (1) enforce model warmup probes during autoscale, (2) add prefix KV caching for common prompts to reduce cold penalty
03:25 Priya: about the KMS/encryption question — did any keys rotate during the incident, and do we need to show key usage logs?
03:33 Samir: no rotation occurred, and we have key usage logs — we'll include the export, but note retention window is 30 days by default for hosted; we can extend on Dedicated or Private deployments
03:50 Maya: can you clarify the Dedicated pilot idea? we are worried about burst traffic to the main route during month end
03:58 Samir: yes — Dedicated pilot would give a small reserved pool for your critical route with predictable warm capacity; we can also set autoscale settings that favor no cold starts for that route. i'll send cost and config options
04:18 Eric: i want to make sure we address monitoring — our alerts didn't trigger on the slow tail because thresholds were set to averages
04:27 Ava: good point — we're recommending a percentile-based alert (p99 > 1.5s for 5m) and an early-warning on queue depth; i'll propose exact prometheus rules in the runbook PR
04:40 Jonas: transcription note, sorry — i keep hearing "K-V cache" as "K-V cash" in the notes, just a funny mis-transcribe but worth cleaning up in the doc
04:49 Samir: noted. any other open risks?
04:55 Priya: from security: if we move to Dedicated pilot, we need explicit audit retention to 180 days and SAML SSO binding verification — also SOC2 docs updated please
05:10 Liam: we'll attach Redwood's SOC2 and the network diagram; Samir will ask security to sign off on the KMS flow for Dedicated
05:22 Maya: on runbook, we want a dry-run — not just tabletop. we want you to trigger a simulated cache eviction and autoscale event to validate playbooks
05:34 Ava: that's fair — we propose a controlled dry-run in a staging mirror of your traffic, or we can do a low-traffic window in prod with feature flags. both have tradeoffs
05:47 Eric: staging mirror preferred; we have a traffic splitter we can use to send a small sample back to a staging model cluster
05:55 Samir: perfect, we'll work on the plan. i'll include exact steps and rollback criteria in the runbook PR
06:05 Maya: one operational ask — please include SLO/SLI language for our internal SLA with product ops, so we can reference it in the contract annex
06:15 Samir: yes, we'll draft SLOs (p50/p95/p99 latency, availability %) and a breach remediation workflow
06:28 Priya: on the audit note — are your audit logs single-tenant for Dedicated? can we get immutable exports?
06:36 Ava: Dedicated gives you customer-isolated log buckets, and we can enable WORM/immutable exports via your S3 settings; we'll include the config options and cost implication
06:50 Jonas: small thing — the user facing errors were 502 vs 504 depending on where the retries fired; we'll capture that in the timeline
07:02 Samir: good catch, add to RCA
07:10 Maya: ok, i want a breakdown of how this would change if we moved to Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted — cost, data residency, and ops burden
07:22 Samir: i'll include a short comparison table in the follow-up email; quick summary: Hosted is fastest to iterate, Dedicated gives reserved capacity + better SLOs and stronger audit controls, Private gives you full network control and longest log retention but longer lead time and ops overhead
07:40 Eric: any blockers on your side to deliver the RCA and runbook?
07:45 Ava: nothing blocker; we need a couple of logs from Celestis — the app retry traces and the router trace for the 11:00-11:45 window
07:55 Maya: i'll get those over by EOD 8/16
08:00 Samir: great. recap: we'll send RCA by 8/18, runbook PR by 8/20, propose Dedicated pilot config by 8/21, and aim for DR dry-run week of 8/31. Questions?
08:12 Priya: none from me, thanks everyone
08:15 Maya: thanks, appreciate it
08:18 Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up in writing

[End of recording]
